statement: For P tending to infinity, integer 1<=k,h1,h2<=P^(1/24), 1<=h<=P^(1/8), and fixed carry-label extensions with offsets frozen on every first-floor gap run, let F be the second-difference branch function, G=F composed with x^(3/2), A(n)=floor(F(floor(n^(3/2)))), c=3k x^(9/8)/4, B=Delta_(2h)c, N=floor B, beta=B-N, and Q=floor(P^(5/16)). The factor e(-Delta_(2h)(cA)) equals sum_{|r|<=Q} a_r(beta)e((N+r-B)G) with total absolute error O(P^(15/16) log P). The coefficient sup norms plus variations sum to O(log P) per refined interval. Retained phases have second derivative O(P^(-3/16) u h P^(-3/4)) for u>=1/2; new boundary costs are O(P^(11/12)) where the total curvature is comparable to the base wave. Proof uses monotone slow-variable counts, O(P^(3/4)) floor-replacement exceptions, and O(P^(7/8)) floor-crossing exceptions. This is a fixed-label reduction, not a bound for all assembled oscillatory sums. The kernel and OOOEE were still open at this branch; subsequent written results J-paper-b-dyadic-kernel-127 and J-paper-b-oooee-mixed-127 supply exponent 127/128 for their specified families. Written proof with exact controls; no independent review or Lean formalization.

Refuted inference: the maximum of the two individual scales of u Delta_(2h1)Y and u' Delta_(2h2)Y certifies mode dominance of their combined phase over the zero-offset anchor in the historical Paper B Theorem 5.3 Step 5(b). With h1=h2=1,u=L,u'=-L, their sum is exactly zero; L comparable to P^(1/4) fits the stated Fourier supports and makes the individual wave scale P^(-1/2) larger than the anchor scale P^(-5/8) at k=1. For h2=2h1,u'=-u/2, the sum is -(u/2) Delta_(2h1)^2 Y. This refutes the dominance inference, not the target exponential-sum estimate, and does not assert that every pair has nonzero coefficient in each application. A bound for the combined signed family is still required.
